newsitem.title: JAPAN: Swiss banks appeal against Japan MOF's tax plan.
newsitem.headline: Swiss banks appeal against Japan MOF's tax plan.

text.p: Three major Swiss banks jointly submitted a petition to Japan's Finance Ministry, urging it to reconsider its plan to end a special law exempting foreigners from a withholding tax on income gains made on Eurobond investments, bank officials said on Friday.
Union Bank of Switzerland, Swiss Bank Corp and Credit Suisse jointly visited the ministry this week to hand over the petition.

"The content of the petition basically called for a need to reconsider the MOF's plan to end the tax exemption law because the actual abolishment could hurt the underwriting market greatly," a senior Credit Suisse official told Reuters.
The ministry was planning to scrap a rule which exempts the withholding tax for non-Japanese residents on income gains made from investments in Eurobonds, including common Euroyen bonds.
The banks asked for the opportunity to discuss the issue with the ministry.
